subject: Clarify: maintenance notation affecting uptime tally for Streamline AI
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@streamline-ai.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discrepancy in uptime credit for 2026-08-13 maintenance window

Hi Naomi,

We were reviewing our monthly uptime statement and noticed the maintenance window logged on 2026-08-13 (10:30–11:10 UTC) didn't result in the expected SLA credit. Our side observed increased error rates and timeouts between 10:38–10:55 UTC that appear to be a partial degradation, not a full outage — and those minutes are being counted against us in the uptime tally.

Can you confirm Redwood's accounting for that window? We have a support trace from our edge (attached screenshot in original ticket) and the exact request IDs if needed. We're trying to reconcile because the discrepancy would change our credited amount materially.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform
Streamline AI

Marissa / Diego — forwarding a billing/uptime question from Streamline. They believe several minutes of degraded responses were counted against their SLA instead of being treated as partial degradation tied to a third-party peering incident (EdgeGrid).

Key asks: 1) Can ops confirm what our availability ledger shows for 2026-08-13 10:30–11:10 UTC (token-level and request-failure windows)? 2) If part of the window was a third-party routing flap, is that excluded under the maintenance/third-party clause, or do we need to apportion credits? 3) If apportionment is needed, propose a concrete credit calculation so I can respond to Liam.

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-08-14T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Discrepancy in uptime credit for 2026-08-13 maintenance window

Naomi / Marissa — I pulled the probe and server logs for the window. Summary:

- Redwood edge probes (region us-west) show elevated 5xx rate starting 2026-08-13T10:37:00Z, peak errors 10:41–10:48Z, and tapering to baseline by 10:56Z. Total span with >1% error delta is ~19 minutes.
- Application-level traces indicate request latencies spiked (p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s) for a subset of prefixes — consistent with an upstream routing flap affecting ~37% of our peered capacity.
- EdgeGrid provided an initial notification indicating a BGP session churn at 10:40Z and a partial route withdrawal until 10:50Z. Their raw trace attached.

Interpretation against SLA: the incident appears to be a third-party upstream routing event that caused partial degradation rather than a platform-wide outage. Per Section 4.2 (Third-party peering exclusions) we can exclude the portion that is unequivocally attributable to EdgeGrid. However, we still have to account for residual degraded requests that are within our routing domain.

Proposed accounting approach:
1) Mark 10:40–10:50Z as primarily third-party-induced; treat that 10 minute block as "third-party exclusion" for the portion of traffic matching EdgeGrid prefixes.
2) For 10:37–10:40Z and 10:50–10:56Z (combined ~9 minutes) treat as partial degradation under our SLO (these minutes are eligible for apportionment/credit).
3) Compute per-prefix traffic fraction and apportion credits to Streamline for the residual degraded minutes only. Using our logs, fraction of affected traffic ~0.37, so effective credited minutes ~= 9 * 0.37 ≈ 3.3 minutes.

I've attached: probe-report-20260814.csv (aggregated probe data), edgegrid-trace-logs.txt (EdgeGrid raw trace).

If legal wants a conservative rounding policy, we can round credited minutes up to nearest whole minute (so 4 minutes).

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: probe-report-20260814.csv (csv stub), edgegrid-trace-logs.txt (text stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: liam@streamline-ai.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: finance@redwood.ai, legal@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-15T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in uptime credit for 2026-08-13 maintenance window

Hi Liam — thanks for flagging and thanks Diego for the analysis.

Short answer: we will issue a partial credit for Streamline AI.

What we're proposing: 
- Per Diego's breakdown, we will exclude the 10:40–10:50Z window where EdgeGrid's routing churn clearly impacted traffic to ~37% of Streamline's requests.
- For the remaining impacted minutes (10:37–10:40Z and 10:50–10:56Z), we'll apportion credits based on the measured traffic fraction; Diego's math gives ~3.3 minutes. Redwood will apply our conservative rounding policy and issue a 4-minute credit toward the August invoice.

Next steps:
1) Finance will draft a credit memo (cc'd) and apply the line item to the August statement.
2) Legal will confirm the wording of the third-party exclusion on the memo; if Streamline wants a different rounding approach, please reply.
3) Ops will keep EdgeGrid engaged for the final trace confirmation (ticket INF-2048).

Liam — does that sound acceptable? If so I'll instruct finance to issue the memo and close this thread.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
